solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stylish appliance France exported for ex-President

parts.note: stylish means cool

indicators.note: exported means sent out of the country, so France's letters leave the appliance

parts.note: a fridge is a kitchen appliance

explanation.surface: A trendy kitchen gadget is shipped out of France for a former head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Calvin Coolidge was the 30th President of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvin Coolidge held the US presidency in the 1920s, so he is a former President.

clue.text: Move within first row threw the French

parts.note: to throw is to cast, and cast is also the past tense
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A chess move along the back rank tossed aside the French opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: Castling is the one chess move where king and rook move together, along the player's first row.
explanation.definitionFit: To castle is a chess move in which king and rook switch places along the back rank.

clue.text: With a pen, mark in lexicon how Napoleon went?

indicators.note: in means the inking goes inside the dictionary

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary, a lexicon
to mark with a pen is to ink

explanation.surface: Someone writes in a dictionary to describe how the French emperor marched.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon is not the emperor but the pig who rules in Orwell's Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigs make grunting noises, so a pig like Orwell's Napoleon would have grunted in this way.

clue.text: Fundamentally popular church south of German city

indicators.note: south of means the church comes below the city in this down clue

parts.note: popular means in fashion, in
Essen is a city in western Germany
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Basically, a well-liked church stands south of a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean basically, at the most essential level of something's nature.

clue.text: Leeks cooked with a thick goo quickly sell

indicators.note: cooked means altered or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dish of leeks in thick gloop sells out fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To go like hot cakes is an idiom for selling fast and in great numbers.

clue.text: Plot with small border covered by hollow crate

indicators.note: covered by means these letters sit inside the hollow crate's letters
hollow means emptied out, leaving only the outside letters of crate

parts.note: a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A conspiracy involving a little edging hidden inside an empty packing case.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a secret plan, which is a synonym of a scheme.

clue.text: Stupid stupid person crowned with crown

indicators.note: crowned with means the crown sits on top of the fool in this down clue

parts.note: CR is the abbreviation for crown
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A dim-witted king wears a crown he does not deserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass means grossly insensitive or obtuse, so it is a synonym of stupid.

clue.text: Smew able to agitate youngsters in flock

indicators.note: to agitate is to stir up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A smew, a kind of duck, is capable of disturbing the young of a flock.
explanation.walkthrough: A smew is a small diving duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewe lambs are young female sheep, the young of a flock of sheep.

clue.text: Being short, local mine hand finally qualified

indicators.note: short means missing its last letter

parts.note: a being is an entity

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of each of local, mine and hand

explanation.surface: A short local miner turns out to be fully qualified.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entitled means having a right or claim to something, so qualified for it.

clue.text: Insecurity of elevated artist held in high esteem

indicators.note: held in means the artist sits inside the esteem

parts.note: preciousness is the state of being highly valued

indicators.note: elevated means raised up, read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: The instability of a celebrated painter who is greatly admired.
explanation.definitionFit: Precariousness is the state of being shaky or unstable, which is a form of insecurity.

clue.text: Coating of spice applied to the Spanish fish

parts.note: the coating of the word spice is its outside letters, S and E, read literally as S AND E
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A cook coats a Spanish fish with a layer of seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of 'spice' are S and E, and the clue wants that read out in full as S-AND-E, followed by EL, Spanish for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand eel is a small slender sea fish that burrows in sand, often eaten by puffins.

clue.text: Spy at back of class makes chemical substance

indicators.note: at back of means the spy comes after the class

parts.note: RE, religious education, is a school class
a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A secret operative sitting at the rear of a schoolroom produces a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is religious education, a lesson in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a compound used to cause or detect a chemical reaction.

clue.text: English city guides announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken aloud, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to guide is to lead, so guides means leads

explanation.surface: Tour guides are being introduced in a city in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, in the north of England.

clue.text: Give impetus to celeb after break with Time

indicators.note: after means the celebrity comes after the break

parts.note: to break a habit is to kick it
a celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: A famous person returns from a holiday and gets things moving again.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick-start something is to boost it into action, like starting a motorbike with a kick.

clue.text: Mean aunt stripped furniture set setter shifted slightly

indicators.note: stripped means the outer letters are removed, leaving the inside of aunt

parts.note: the middle letters of aunt

indicators.note: shifted slightly means the setter's letter moves a short way along within the furniture

parts.note: a chair and table make a set of furniture
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: An unkind relative strips the furniture while the compiler moves things about.
explanation.walkthrough: In CHAIRTABLE the I moves one place to the right, giving CHARITABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mean in spirit is a synonym of lacking generosity or kindness toward others.

clue.text: Stretches in starts of triathlon usually in this?

definitions.text: Stretches in starts of triathlon usually in this?

indicators.note: in means the stretches go inside those first letters
starts of means the first letter of each of the next four words

parts.note: racks stretch, as on the medieval rack

explanation.surface: A triathlete warms up with stretches, dressed for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracksuit is the loose two-piece outfit athletes wear for warming up and training.

clue.text: Aircrew regularly on jump, as was Shackleton

indicators.note: on means the first part sits above the second in this down clue
regularly means every other letter of aircrew

parts.note: a bound is a jump

explanation.surface: A flight crew jumps in turn, like an explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest Shackleton's ship Endurance was trapped in Antarctic pack ice in 1915.
explanation.definitionFit: Shackleton's ship was held fast by frozen sea, trapped and unable to move.

clue.text: Mould exposed on dead hoofed animal

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: mould is a fungus
late means dead, as in the late king

explanation.surface: Fungus found growing on the carcass of a hoofed beast.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungulate is a mammal with hoofs, such as a horse, cow or deer.

clue.text: Sister's place by island lake is nothing special

definitions.note: a phrase that works as the adjective ordinary

parts.note: a nun, or Sister, lives in a convent
Iona is a Scottish island

explanation.surface: A nunnery beside an island lake turns out to be fairly ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Something conventional follows accepted norms, so it is ordinary and unremarkable.

clue.text: Trip in exercise on river clipper

indicators.note: on means the first part sits above the river in this down clue
in means the trip sits inside the exercise

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
a trip can be a run, a short journey

explanation.surface: A jog during a workout by the river, perhaps with a fast sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipper' suggests the sailing ship, but here it is something that clips.
explanation.definitionFit: A pruner is a gardener or tool that clips and trims branches.

clue.text: Officer guards rear unit NASA uses

indicators.note: guards means the officer surrounds the rear

parts.note: PC is a police constable, an officer
arse is British slang for backside

explanation.surface: A policeman protects the rear of an object used by the space agency.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsec is an astronomical distance measure of about 3.26 light years.

clue.text: Rubes slag off style of music

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Country bumpkins insult a musical genre, perhaps the very one they play.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluegrass is a type of American country music from Appalachia, played on banjo and fiddle.

clue.text: Mark turned ashen in auditorium

indicators.note: in an auditorium the words are heard, so this is a sound-alike

parts.note: to turn ashen is to go grey, so greyed

explanation.surface: A performer goes pale in the theatre on getting a poor review mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A grade is a mark given for work in school, such as an A or B.

clue.text: Indian dish Mo divided amongst ship heading west

indicators.note: heading west means read right to left in an across clue
divided means the two letters of Mo are split up, the O moving along past another letter
amongst means the letters of Mo go among the ship's letters

parts.note: an ark is a ship, as Noah's
Mo is taken as written, its two letters going into the ship
the O of Mo, the letter that moves

explanation.surface: Mo shares a curry with the crew of a boat sailing west.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo is not kept whole: its two letters end up apart, one each side of a letter of the ship, before the whole is read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A korma is a mild creamy curry from South Asian cuisine.

clue.text: Section of Verdun:A War Exhibition is in the dark

definitions.note: a phrase that works as the adjective ignorant

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A visitor to a First World War exhibition about Verdun knows nothing about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the dark is an idiom for lacking knowledge, the same as being ignorant of something.

clue.text: Note about housing one of 5 in 17s

definitions.note: 17-down is UNGULATE, so this is the plural ungulates; horses and their kin are examples

indicators.note: housing means holding the quin inside
about here means facing round the other way, so the word for note is read backwards

parts.note: to note is to see
a quin is one of five children born together, a quintuplet

explanation.surface: A musical note concerning one of five siblings among a herd of hoofed animals.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a cross-reference to 5-across, but here it simply means five; '17s' does point to 17-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses, donkeys and zebras are hoofed mammals, so the equine family is an example of the ungulates.

clue.text: Hawk briefly follows the Austrian car?

indicators.note: follows means the shortened hawk comes after the Austrian word

parts.note: Austrians speak German, and die is a German word for the

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to hawk goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: A street vendor trails an Austrian, perhaps trying to sell them a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is a vehicle with a diesel engine, so a car is one example; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Old Crete is oddly mysterious

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ancient Crete has a strange, enigmatic air.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means understood only by a small inner circle, hence obscure or arcane.
